column3: A causal exploration coupling would need to turn supercritical space-time percolation into unavoidable detection for every past-adapted continuous target; full-future block estimates do not establish this equality. Locate the exact past-information definition before any coupling proof; dimension one and adaptation quantifiers cannot be dropped.

Mansour–Shattuck arXiv:1207.3755 Theorem 3.3 supplies the full recurrence with initial values 1,1,2, and the subsequent generating-function calculation identifies height-five Dyck paths. A new bijection would be an alternative proof of a public result.

Source Conjecture 1 asks for 2/log2(n); Theorem 2 gives only 1/log2(n). Spencer disproved Bondy's constant-one assertion, not this logarithmic assertion. Doubling the inductive bound requires a new invariant; a normalized-weight cycle LP could test a fixed graph but would not prove all n.

Source introduction explicitly reports Schulz's counterexample to generalized Auslander–Reiten over a self-injective quantum exterior algebra with parameter not a root of unity; source relates its derived formulation to that module assertion. No new counterexample credit; the cited module's complete resolution has not been audited here.

Full elementary invariance for all MM++-preserving forcings is stronger than Sigma1 absoluteness. The source identifies an amalgamation obstacle combining Lemma 4.2 with Theorem 3.1. Requires forcing and large-cardinal machinery, not a finite certificate; park.

Equal longest right-translation cycles allow block permutations that the strict-length proof excludes. Need a centralizer automorphism fixing the final block pointwise for every natural reordering, not just a relabeling of one quandle. Finite operation-table enumeration would supply instances only; successor and definition audit remain.

The second discrete difference of maximal inscribed disk-polygon area is required negative for every radius and every even n as well as odd n. Circumscribed convexity and the odd-index theorem do not control even maximizers. Need an extremizer formula or a variational comparison; numerical regular polygons are insufficient.

Projection point counting explains allowable offsets but not why every exponentially dense minor-closed class eventually has that structure. Source Conjecture 1.5 would imply the target; proving it needs an unbounded-rank structure theorem. Do not replace arbitrary classes by representable examples.

Source explicitly says Conjecture 1.2 is proved by Theorem 1.3. Its finite range q<=8192 therefore offers no new-result credit. Arc coordinates and the full computational certificate were not reconstructed; a repeat sweep would reproduce public computation.

A generic determinant argument must show that each full-rank active-constraint pattern has no forced degeneracy in arbitrary dimensions. Source suggests finite graph-pattern determinants for fixed dimensions, but their nonvanishing is the unresolved bridge. One polytope pair is not generic all-parameter coverage.

Need both asymptotic bounds uniformly in n for each fixed positive k<=l'. Middle-level packing gives a lower-bound route; the trace constraints require the matching polynomial saving in the upper bound. Source's theorem for l'<k is a different regime; no finite n calculation establishes Theta.

One extremum gives only one side of the contracting-homotopy argument. Need a chain-level split over Z proving exactly the two gcd torsion types in every degree and every finite skew lattice. Smith forms for small lattices are instances; no general contraction or exclusion of additional torsion obtained.

Need exact K4-minus tiling at codegree n/2-1 for every multiple of four above eight. An absorbing proof with epsilon slack cannot settle the boundary or small residual n; asymptotic source bound does not suffice. Successor audit needed before any SAT enumeration of small cases.

Need supersaturation just one edge above an unknown Turan extremum, for every fixed s and all sufficiently large n. A deletion count must exclude configurations with a unique clique without assuming an extremal classification. Small-n failures cannot refute this eventual assertion; park.

Requires a uniform spanning embedding theorem for bounded-degree forbidden families and an exact extremal remainder; F(v) is source-specific link notation and must be reconciled before use. Treating it as ordinary vertex deletion or fixing one F would change scope. Deep embedding program, not a small certificate.

Exact recursion for every fixed dimension and sufficiently large primes needs a structural inverse zero-sum theorem, not just the (d-1+gamma)p estimate. Source proves an asymptotic dimension-three result. Small prime exceptions are expressly allowed; bounded search cannot refute eventual equality.

Primary question itself asks to define a suitable linearization. No fixed admissibility predicate is supplied by the record, so maximization is not yet an exact formal endpoint. Transfinite learning-tree ranks and de Jongh–Parikh analogies do not choose that predicate. HOLD for definition gap, no wording-fix credit.

For arbitrary finite scoring octal rules and each auxiliary heap m, must prove an eventual period exactly dividing 2k. A max-minus recurrence route needs bounded state differences and eventual stabilization; observed periodic prefixes do not prove those bounds. Source conjecture spans all rule strings; park without an invariant.

Explicit nilpotent-rank-three modules show attainability, not an upper bound on every finitely generated module. Need a central L(0) polynomial relation on all blocks or a classification of indecomposable extensions. Screening constructions do not exclude length-four Jordan chains; deep VOA dependencies.

Iteration must preserve connectedness, the complete approximation conclusion, and four reflections outside measure 1/n simultaneously. Connecting mirror gadgets can create extra reflected rays of positive measure; source's suggestion of iteration leaves this error estimate open. Requires geometric measure and billiard dependency audit.

Modular divisibility might rule out tail progressions but must cover all admissible d and all tail starts and lengths. Prime-order obstruction does not automatically extend to composite k; a finite prime search cannot certify the infinite tail. Need source definition of GAP occurrences and a covering congruence proof.

Need identities for every r not divisible by three expressing all degree-r products of twisted-cubic quadrics in J, plus noncontainment for r-1. Source only illustrates r=2 using a transvectant identity. Groebner computations for fixed r do not prove the uniform syzygy identity; park.

Finite box classifications through seven do not classify lattice polygons for unbounded m. Need extremal vertex/Picard-rank structure, then uniqueness, smoothness and minimum degree jointly. Any isolated smooth polygon or classification at m=8 is only an instance; no full-scope reduction obtained.

Source S_d is a special ball-derived set, requiring definition fidelity before volume reasoning. Fubini bounds on line sections and componentwise isodiametry do not reach the proposed sharp value simultaneously. Widely separated components still interact through lines; no valid all-d,n extremizer found.

Monotonicity of bosonic binding requires strict energy separation for every smaller electron count, not monotonicity of energy alone. Zhislin's range leaves the excess-charge regime untouched. Removing a particle can move a state to a continuum threshold; requires Coulomb spectral analysis, no finite witness route.

Residue classes and coordinate compression suggest k^(w-1), but must preserve pairwise 1-crossing while avoiding k-crossing in all dimensions. Ranked families and w<=3 are proved internally; the displayed theorem is not full-scope. Closest published successor may extend w=4; not audited, so no novelty clearance.

Keusch arXiv:2303.02611v4 Theorem 1 assigns weights 1,2,3 to every graph without a K2 component, which includes every assigned connected simple graph of order at least three. Theorem statement inspected; complete proof and dependencies not audited. Reproving this receives zero credit.

Symmetrizing an approximant reduces the search to n+1 values but its Fourier L1 norm still involves Krawtchouk transforms and cancellations. Need a dual witness with only logarithmic loss, not the exact-norm theorem alone. Constant-function logarithmic endpoints require definition care but yield no substantive credit.

Need classify all integer m and also exclude three colors in every higher dimension. Parity reductions and explicit modular colorings establish families but no universal obstruction outside them. A finite four-chromatic unit-distance subgraph may handle one m only; number-theoretic reduction of all m is missing.

The inequality and equality classification over all Fano dimensions require Mori-contraction structure. Source settles n<=4; products of projective spaces realize equality but do not exclude other contractions in arbitrary dimension. No short full-dimensional bridge; park.

Can model clique colorings by measures on independent transversals with avoidance constraints at outside vertices. Independent uniform clique permutations need not leave one unit of available measure at every outside vertex. Need global correlated coupling or an exact infeasible LP witness satisfying graph hypotheses; no such witness constructed.

An affine space underlying a homogeneous action need not be special for its stabilizer. Need control of torsors for P_deltaN acting on gamma N/N^C using canonical parabolics, not just an affine-coordinate parametrization. Source's subsequent trace-formula program and field hypotheses require dependency audit; park.

Flatten to a p-by-4 binary matrix. GL(p) row operations reduce to its row subspace of F2^4, so all p>=4 reduce to finitely many subspaces under GL(2)xGL(2). The bounded orbit check below gives ten nonzero subspace orbits, but full Table 5 ranks and lexicographic minima still need comparison. This is a routine stabilization reduction; no eligible discovery claim or novelty clearance.

The source proves a reduction from Boolean block sensitivity to lattice dimension, whose direction does not make Huang's Boolean theorem imply the lattice assertion. Need a reverse reduction with sensitivity polynomial independent of min-width. Arbitrarily distant first blue axis points block a naive finite-cube restriction; successor gap explicit.

Huang arXiv:1907.00847v2 Theorem 1.5 states bs(f)<=s(f)^4 for every Boolean f. It combines the signed-cube bound with a degree/block-sensitivity theorem. Statement and dependency description inspected, not a full proof audit; it settles the exact target publicly.

The source constructs arbitrary p-gradient values; absolute rank gradient takes the infimum over all finite-index subgroups, not only p-power restrictions. Must control every finite quotient or prove equality of these gradients for the constructed group. This bridge is not supplied by the abstract; no transfer credit.

Dujmovic–Esperet–Joret–Walczak–Wood arXiv:1904.05269 Theorem 1 gives pi(G)<=768 for every planar graph. Product-structure and strongly nonrepetitive-coloring dependencies explain the mechanism. The full external product-structure proof was not audited; the assigned existence assertion is already public.

DDS provides an upper-bound construction; optimality needs matching lower bounds for every k,n. Finite book-order SAT or exact crossing counts cannot prove the two-parameter conjecture. Known small-n equality and adjacent-order propagation are insufficient; closest successor/prior scope remains unaudited.

Source proves generalized MGL for finite abelian 2-groups, using subgroup-compatible entropy minimizers. Odd-primary factors need a new extremizer analysis; convexity of each candidate branch does not imply convexity of their lower envelope. Exact or interval-certified entropy witnesses on a small odd group are a possible test, not executed.

One way fixes occupancy counts but the union-of-disks area is piecewise smooth with changing overlap combinatorics. Need strict concavity or a certified polygon with two distinct local maxima in one way, after quotienting disk labels. Numerical optimizers alone cannot distinguish symmetry copies or certify local maximality.

Brick-generation discharging must produce linearly many degree-three vertices, whereas source only guarantees a linear number of degree-at-most-four vertices. A degree-four-only chain may defeat naive charging. Checking small bicritical graphs is not a proof of a uniform positive fraction; park.

A counterexample must be ideal, minimally nonpacking under every proper minor, and have transversal number at least three. Testing nonpacking alone misses ideality and minor minimality. Source's affine-plane reformulation suggests LP-duality certificates, but no small ideal obstruction surviving all these tests obtained.

The lower-bound parity construction covers every k; upper bound needs show any codegree above one half forces a simplex in arbitrary uniformity. Density calculations and k=2 graph arguments do not extend to k=3 or larger. This is an unbounded extremal program, not a finite certificate.

Immediately after Conjecture 5.10 the primary source reports Eremin's counterexample to the tour formula and a repaired multitour formula. Ordinary tours cannot represent every fractional dual optimum; reusing a multitour theorem changes the target. Counterexample body not independently reconstructed; no novelty credit.

Exact parity/divisibility barriers must characterize all extremizers for every k/2<=ell<=k-1 and sufficiently large n divisible by k. Absorption usually gives slack while stability must handle equality. Source's delta(n,k,ell) definition and later exact-threshold successors need further audit; park rather than guessing a threshold.

Source gives a polynomial-in-t bound, not the record's claimed exponential-only bound. Full target needs a constant depending only on r times t; sunflower or greedy arguments currently lose powers of t. Fixing r=2 or finitely many t is an instance; closest later rainbow-matching results not cleared.

Random deletion of repeated-distance triples/quads yields the source's N^(1/3)/log(N) scale. Reaching almost N^(1/2) requires a stronger incidence structure or independent-set mechanism. Grids give upper obstructions but do not refute the epsilon-loss lower bound; no all-point-set certificate route.

At r=1 a 2-regular bipartite mask is a union of cycles, and disconnected components permit independent factor rescalings, preventing global completion. This suggests an omitted-rank qualification, but is a domain/scope issue expressly ineligible for credit. For r>=2 need generic completion-matroid rigidity with random deletion of r^2 edges; no general proof or successor clearance.

D is total variation between two different pair-sampling laws. Symmetry alone does not force one large and n equal small probabilities. Need a smoothing inequality excluding extrema with three unequal masses for all n, including nonsmooth sign regions; finite rational simplex checks would be only evidence.

Uniqueness must be read in the sorted-probability convention of primary equation (17), so permuting colors is not an eligible counterexample. Beyond the existence target need strictness in every smoothing step and a unique one-variable maximum for all n. Three-color algebra does not establish arbitrary-color uniqueness.
